reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it presents a project review that explains how viewers could participate in the Nakama Coin presale and identifies itself as educational, not financial advice. It discusses presale bonuses, buyback and value-appreciation claims, and wallet-to-swap instructions as project information and purchasing guidance. Those claims do not by themselves show deceptive conduct, and the video also instructs viewers to verify the contract address.

opening.argument: Judge, the promised benefit and the requested purchase are presented together. The speaker says the buyback mechanism means reduced supply, price appreciation and higher value, then urges viewers to join the earlier sale stage for extra tokens. This is more than an explanation of how presales work: the claimed upside is tied to a specific buying decision, and the speaker offers a link to act on it.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling it educational does not resolve the concern raised by the speaker's own wording. The defense cites the bonus as project information, but the speaker goes further and tells viewers to join stage one. Contract-address verification can help identify which token is being purchased; it does not verify that the claimed appreciation will occur.

citations.quote: so be a part of stage one so that you can get by one dollar 28 750
they reduce supply, price appreciation, more usage, more fees, more buybacks higher value and repeat

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The speaker does encourage participation, but neither the bonus nor the buyback description establishes deception. The video expressly warns viewers to analyze the project before deciding, and the stated appreciation is a description of the project's proposed mechanism, not evidence that returns are guaranteed or that purchasers will be defrauded.

opening.argument: Judge, consider the signals in combination. The sale page advertises an early-buyer return of up to 2.875x at launch alongside time-limited bonus stages, while the speaker repeats the larger first-stage bonus and urges viewers to take it. The same presentation describes a buyback cycle leading to price appreciation. A projected launch return, a reason to buy earlier, and an upward-value narrative make the purchase pitch look misleadingly confident, even though the return is not certain.

citations.quote: in stage one bonus you will get 15 percent extra token in stage two bonus you will get five percent extra token so be a part of stage one

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense treats the bonus and value claims as neutral project details. But the displayed early-buyer ROI claim gives those details a return-focused meaning, and the speaker's stage-one invitation makes timing consequential. A disclaimer that this is not financial advice does not remove the impression created by that combination.

this video is for educational and informational purpose only i am not a financial adviser this is not a financial advice

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These are reasons for caution, not proof of a scam. The displayed figure is qualified as an upper bound, and the spoken buyback discussion reports the project's proposed token economics. The video also explicitly says investments involve risk. No cited evidence establishes that the displayed projection is knowingly false or that a promised return is guaranteed.

All investments involve risk, and past performance does not guarantee future results.

opening.argument: Judge, the review framing should be tested against what the video actually asks viewers to do. It walks them through obtaining BNB, then shows a wallet connection and how to pay. The speaker offers a launchpad link so viewers can participate. The description also provides a presale link and promotion contact details. In that context, the discussion of the project's buyback-driven price appreciation functions as part of a purchase pitch, not merely detached market commentary.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense is right that purchasing instructions alone do not prove deception. Its account is incomplete, though: this walkthrough ends with an offered participation link, while the video presents a mechanism said to produce price appreciation. Verifying a contract address addresses mistaken identity, not whether the investment case used to steer viewers toward that address is sound.
